title: California's 14th Congressional District Special Election, 2026
description: A special election is underway in California's 14th Congressional District following the resignation of former Rep. Eric Swalwell, who left Congress after ending his gubernatorial campaign amid sexual misconduct allegations. The district, wholly contained within Alameda County, leans strongly Democratic. A nonpartisan top-two special primary was held on June 16, 2026, with 11 candidates on the ballot; if no candidate receives a majority, a special general election will be held on August 18, 2026. Separately, the regularly scheduled primary for the full term beginning January 2027 was held June 2, 2026, and the general election is November 3, 2026.
polling_note: No verified public opinion polls for this specific special election were found. Early results from the June 2, 2026 regular primary showed State Sen. Aisha Wahab leading with 34% and former Dublin Mayor Melissa Hernandez with 16% (ABC7, June 3, 2026).

candidates.name: Aisha Wahab
candidates.summary: Aisha Wahab is a California State Senator representing the 10th Senate District. She was the leading vote-getter in the June 2, 2026 regular primary for this congressional seat and is a candidate in the June 16 special primary. Wahab is endorsed by the California Democratic Party and is widely viewed as the frontrunner in the race to succeed former Rep. Eric Swalwell.

forecast.rationale: No verified public opinion polls exist for this special election, which depresses confidence. The district is wholly within Alameda County and described as strongly Democratic, giving any Democratic nominee an overwhelming partisan advantage (~95%+ party win probability). Among a field of at least 11 candidates, State Sen. Aisha Wahab is the strongest individual contender: she led the June 2 regular primary for the concurrent full-term race with 34%, well ahead of the next Democrat (former Dublin Mayor Melissa Hernandez at 16%), and she has the endorsement of the California Democratic Party. The special primary was held June 16, 2026; with a fragmented field, it is plausible no candidate received a majority, forcing an August 18 runoff. In a likely runoff between a Democrat and a Republican, the Democrat would be heavily favored; even in a Democrat-vs-Democrat runoff, Wahab's primary performance and institutional support make her the likeliest winner. However, the absence of special-election-specific polling and the large candidate field introduce uncertainty about the exact runoff configuration and final margin, hence a medium confidence rating.
